chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله bequeathed solely to ʿAlī عليه السلام, and ʿAlī عليه السلام bequeathed jointly to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, and al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was his Imam.

So a man entered upon al-Ḥasan عليه السلام on the Day of ʿArafah while he was eating the midday meal, and al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام was fasting. Then, after al-Ḥasan عليه السلام passed away, he came and entered upon al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام on the Day of ʿArafah while he was eating the midday meal, and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام was fasting.
So the man said to him: Indeed, I entered upon al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while he was eating the midday meal and you were fasting; then I entered upon you and you are not fasting.

He said: Indeed, al-Ḥasan عليه السلام was an Imam, so he broke his fast lest his fasting be taken as a sunnah (prophetic tradition) and the people follow him in that. Then when he was taken, I was the Imam, so I wanted that my fasting not be taken as a sunnah (prophetic tradition), such that the people would follow me in it.

key_terms.إِمَاماً: the divinely designated leader whose practice is followed
key_terms.سُنَّةً: a normative religious practice that people may adopt and follow
key_terms.مُفْطِرٌ: not fasting; having broken or left the fast
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah, a significant day associated with hajj and recommended worship

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ḥasan and Imam al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام refrain from fasting on the Day of ʿArafah in this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the succession of authority from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام and then to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام. It also shows the Imam’s deliberate practice regarding fasting on the Day of ʿArafah so that his personal act would not be assumed by people to be an established sunnah (prophetic tradition).
